  Requirement: However, the PR also introduces a changelog fragment whose body accurately describes the actual poller behavior and test on disk.
  Expected change site: `changelog.d/6914-security-pass-cap-low-test.md` (the whole file), and probably a new fragment that accurately describes the deliverable of this PR.
  Evidence of absence:
  - The fragment's headline reads "The orchestrate-poll test for a low-severity finding at the security-pass `keep_fixing` cap now expects the project to fail, as the poller does." The actual test `test_security_pass_cap_converts_low_keep_fixing_to_advisory` (tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:6649-6705) asserts `latest_state["status"] == "complete"` (line 6669), `latest_state["security_pass_status"] == "passed"` (line 6670), that a waiver is recorded (lines 6674-6680), and that an `ai:security` advisory follow-up issue is created (lines 6681-6685). It explicitly asserts `"ai:security-pass-failed" not in result["tracking_labels"]` (line 6686) and `"SECURITY_PASS_FAILED" not in combined_log` (line 6693). The test expects the project to PASS, not to fail.
  - The fragment body says "Since #6539 the cap converts a low or medium `keep_fixing` decision to `fail`". `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:7376-7382` does the opposite: when `keep_fixing_capped` is true, decisions whose `finding.severity` is `low` or `medium` and whose action is `keep_fixing` are rewritten to action `accept_with_followup` and prefixed with `[keep_fixing capped after <N> judge round(s); converted to advisory follow-up]`. The matching waiver-and-follow-up record path is reached only when, after the rewrite, no `keep_fixing` rows remain (lines 7395-7397, 7418). `agents.md:2010` records the same rule ("after verdict normalization the poller rewrites low/medium `keep_fixing` decisions to `accept_with_followup`"). The historical record for #6906 (referenced in `changelog.d/6947-heal-scope-failing-test-subjects.md` line 4, `docs/plans/prepush-affected-test-gate-plan.md` line 100, `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:6654,6709`, `agents.md:997`, and `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:2218`) confirms that #6906 restored the advisory rule that #6549 had briefly flipped; the failed heal PRs #6907 and #6916 attempted to rewrite the test to match the obsolete fail rule, which is the same content this fragment still asserts.
  - The fragment body says "The test, renamed `test_security_pass_cap_converts_low_keep_fixing_to_fail`". A grep for `_to_fail` in `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` returns no such test; `test_security_pass_cap_converts_low_keep_fixing_to_advisory` is the only test at that signature and it is still named exactly that on line 6649.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
